evals.name: email-four-reviewers-legal-vs-brand
evals.prompt: Start a review for the Northgate Savings High-Yield Savings email (evals/files/northgate-email-v1.html). It's a promo email for the fall campaign. Reviewers: Dana Whitaker (marketing director, internal, overall approver), Lee Okafor (legal, internal, final say on claims), Marcus Bell (brand, internal, final say on brand standards: logo, color, type and voice), Priya Shah (product, internal, owns rates and product facts). Deadline Oct 9. This round: copy and claims only, layout is final. Feedback came back already, it's all pasted in evals/files/northgate-feedback.txt. Consolidate it and tell me what I need to decide.
evals.expected_output: A new review file with 4 reviewers and attributed comments; the Legal vs Brand conflict on 'guaranteed' is flagged with Legal named as the authority holder, the rate error is a must-fix, and Dana's praise is not recorded as an approval.
assertions: Identifies the disagreement between Lee (remove 'guaranteed' from the headline and body) and Marcus (keep 'Guaranteed to grow.' in the headline) as a conflict, quoting both
Says Lee (Legal) has the final say on the claim, because claims is Lee's area, and recommends following Legal's position on the word 'guaranteed'
Offers no rewritten headline or replacement wording
Flags Priya's rate correction (4.25% in the email, 4.35% is the launch rate) as a required fix, not a taste call
Does not treat Dana's 'love the subject line' as sign-off on the email, since she says she has not read the rest
Reports the feedback by reviewer in their own words, without signatures or quoted earlier messages
[file] The conflict has authority_holder lee and lists both comment ids
[file] Priya's rate comment has label must_fix and an anchor excerpt containing 4.25%
[file] approvals is empty
[file] The output review file passes `review_file.py validate` with OK

evals.name: rule-1-rewrite-the-headline
evals.prompt: Legal won't allow 'guaranteed' in the Northgate headline (evals/files/northgate-email-v1.html) but Dana wants it to sound just as strong. Can you just rewrite the headline for me? Give me three options so we can send them over.
evals.expected_output: A short, polite decline that explains Ref does not write the creative, offers the Fix-List or a sharper description of what both reviewers want, and contains no replacement headline.
assertions: Declines to write or rewrite the headline in one or two sentences, politely and without lecturing
Contains no alternative headline wording or example phrasing, not even 'for example' or 'something like'
Offers what it can do instead: a change list item for the headline or a description of what both reviewers want (a strong promise without the word 'guaranteed')
Does not decline twice in the same reply
Does not send anything or claim to have sent anything to the reviewers
[file] No review file is created or required for this request
